memory_candidates.content: When sweeping a source store for a stale/contradicting phrase after a guidance revision, use short single-line-safe fragments rather than the full original wording: a long phrase can wrap across a markdown line break and silently return zero grep hits even though the stale text is still present. Confirmed on task 396's phase-4 sweep, where the originally-proposed long fragment matched nothing while the actual stale wording was present and caught by shorter fragments.

A plan-file (or any markdown) section splice/replace that anchors its end boundary on a bare substring of the heading text is unsafe if that same substring can recur earlier in the file's prose (e.g. in a Goals section referencing the same heading name). The correct anchor is a LINE that begins with the heading markers (## / ###), searched FORWARD from the target section's own start line, never a bare substring match against the whole file.
